summary: Only on 1h, and mostly in uptrends. Across BTC, ETH and SOL, the default setting beat random on 1h at 20 candles only, and did the same as random on 4h and daily. The result that holds up is the uptrend split: above the 200-day SMA, the default 1h setting beat random by 1.07% after 20 candles and still beat it at 50. In downtrends it showed nothing.

verdicts.use: Buying the crack below the base on 1h (default)
verdicts.text: Beat random by 0.47% after 20 candles across BTC, ETH and SOL. At 10, 50 and 100 candles it was the same as random.
Beat random by 0.95% after 20 candles, at that horizon only. Above the 200-day SMA it beat random by 1.97% and held at 50 candles, while below it it was the same as random.

verdicts.use: Buying the crack on 4h and daily (default)
verdicts.text: The default did the same as random on 4h and on daily candles.

verdicts.use: Bigger base or pump on 4h (base 72, pump 5%)
verdicts.text: Base 72 and pump 5% did worse than random on 4h, by 1.17% and 1.1%. Each rests on one crash: May 7–13, 2022 for base 72 and Jun 10–19, 2022 for pump 5%.

notes: On 1h, the default base 36, pump 3%, crack 3% gave 4,239 entries in 432 separate moves. Twenty candles later they were 0.47% ahead of random entries, above a luck band that tops out at 0.33%. The gap holds without its strongest day, Feb 28, 2021 (18 entries), but disappears at 10, 50 and 100 candles. A deeper crack of 5% fires about half as often and beat random by 0.95%, with the same single-horizon catch. Pump 1%, crack 1% fires more than two and a half times as often and did the same as random.

The 1h result comes from uptrends. With the pair above its 200-day SMA, the default beat random by 1.07%, crack 5% by 1.97% and pump 5% by 1.5%. Each holds without the Feb 28, 2021 day and also shows at 50 candles. Below the SMA the same three settings landed at -0.01%, 0.25% and -0.1%, all the same as random.

Two other 1h variants looked better in uptrends but rest on one day. Pump 1%, crack 1% beat random by 0.3% only because of signals on Feb 28, 2021. Base 72 beat it by 0.84% only because of signals on May 23, 2021. Without that day, each is the same as random.

On 4h the default landed 0.83% behind random, inside the luck band. Base 72 looked worse than random, but only because of signals on May 7–13, 2022, during the Terra collapse. Pump 5% looked worse only because of signals on Jun 10–19, 2022, around the Celsius withdrawal freeze, and both ETH and BTC rest on that stretch.

One 4h result does not rest on a single crash. Below the 200-day SMA, pump 1%, crack 1% did 1.07% worse than random after 20 candles, and also at 10 candles. It stays worse without its strongest stretch on May 6–13, 2022, and is the same as random at 50 and 100 candles. On daily the default gave 42 moves and was the same as random. On each coin alone and in uptrends it had fewer than 30, too few to judge.

For a long QFL bot, the crack below the base told you something only on 1h with the pair above its 200-day SMA. That makes a trend filter beside the QFL start condition the combination to test, not the crack alone. The drift showed at 20 and 50 candles and not at 10, so a take profit sized for a quick bounce gets nothing from it. In downtrends on 4h, shallow cracks did worse than random, and DCA orders there kept buying a base that was still breaking.
